statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 85% (high). Every hour of the published horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists to score.
recommendation: Tail is published at a closed-venue floor and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON across the horizon. No danger window is published, because no venue quotes at any point in the window and there is therefore no evidence-based interval to flag. The material forward checkpoints all sit outside it: the Sunday 22:00 UTC CME restart, roughly nineteen hours after the final published hour, where Friday's hawkish payroll repricing and any accumulated US-Iran developments would be expressed as a single gap rather than as an observable path; the US Labor Day holiday on Monday 7 September, which delays the first full US cash session to Tuesday 8 September; and the resumption of the macro calendar with PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC meeting. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state, and later assessment cycles will score the restart once a live price path exists.
headline: Nasdaq-100 sits idle at 29,544.15 with CME futures settled since Friday 21:00 UTC; the full 24-hour horizon falls inside the weekend halt, so Tail is published at a closed-venue floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 0.21% from a 29,482.30 prior close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered into the cash close. Retracement occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The August employment report printed 162,000 nonfarm payrolls against a consensus near 56,000, with the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1%; short-dated Treasury yields rose and reporting placed the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting at 58.4%, up from 49.4% the previous day. The broad tape softened on that repricing, with the Dow down 0.51%, the S&P 500 down 0.38% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.29%, yet the Nasdaq-100 finished higher because Friday's internals were split rather than one-way: semiconductors led strongly while several large-cap software names and Tesla fell, Tesla by about 6% after its Cybercab launch event and an NHTSA audit query. Split internals of that kind reduce directional conviction rather than amplify Tail. The latest H.15 column shows the 2-year at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77%, while the VIX closed at 14.53, up 1.47% inside a 13.80-14.58 range, leaving no volatility stress into the settle. Energy remains the standing risk premium: WTI traded near $91.48 and Brent near $96.28 after weekly gains close to 10% and 7.6%, driven by renewed US-Iran military exchanges in the seventh month of that conflict and Strait of Hormuz transits running far below the pre-war baseline. CME equity index futures settled at 21:00 UTC on Friday, so no live price path exists for NQ futures or the NAS100 CFD at this assessment and none will exist until the Sunday 22:00 UTC restart, roughly nineteen hours after the final published hour. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday, so the first full US cash session follows on 8 September. Tail is therefore held at a closed-venue floor across the horizon, while Stress drifts from 38 to 44 to reflect two days of hawkish rate-path and geopolitical exposure carried unpriced across the halt, and Confidence decays from 85 to 77 as Friday's verified evidence set ages.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the second half of the August payroll session and the first seven hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 14-17% with Stress climbing from 53 to 62 through the pre-release Asian and European hours, peaked at Tail 24% and Stress 76% in the 12:00 UTC release hour under an event/whipsaw mode as the 162,000 payroll print landed against a consensus near 56,000, then decayed steadily through the US cash session as the index fully retraced its highs and recovered. By 20:00 UTC Tail was back to 12% with Stress at 48%, and from the 21:00 UTC CME settle the assessment moved to a closed-venue floor of Tail 5% and Stress 38%, held through the overnight hours. No hour required a mapped state beyond WATCH.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 38% to a horizon maximum of 44%, still inside the moderate band, reflecting hawkish September rate-path pricing and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz energy premium carried unpriced across two days. Confidence decays from 85% to 77% as Friday's verified evidence ages. The Sunday 22:00 UTC restart, the Monday US Labor Day holiday and the 8 September cash session all fall beyond the final published hour and will be scored by later cycles.
